title: Constructibility of the reduced geometric fibre locus
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Assume $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For each $t\in T$ let $X_{\bar t}$ be the geometric fibre obtained by base change to a chosen algebraic closure of $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Then the subset $E_f=\{t\in T\mid X_{\bar t}\text{ is reduced}\}$ is constructible in $T$ [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Reduced means that every local ring has no nonzero nilpotents [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Empty geometric fibres count as reduced. Neither flatness of $f$ nor a Noetherian hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0579 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-constructible), with topology.tex Tag 053W (lemma-collate-constructible) on a finite affine cover of the qcqs base. The geometric-fibre convention is equivalent to geometric reducedness by varieties.tex Tag 035X (lemma-geometrically-reduced), (2) iff (6), in positive characteristic and Tag 020I (lemma-perfect-reduced) in characteristic zero.
